u3.intro: Tiempos de pasado: cuándo usar cada uno y cómo hablar de hábitos pasados.

sections.title: Past simple
sections.explain: Acciones terminadas en un momento concreto, secuencias de hechos en una historia, hábitos y estados pasados. Forma enfática con did + infinitivo.
examples: Sony and Philips developed the CD in 1979.
I did enjoy the concert — honestly!

sections.title: Past simple vs present perfect
sections.explain: Past simple = tiempo terminado (yesterday, in 2019, ago, when I was…). Present perfect = periodo hasta ahora o resultado presente (ever, never, yet, so far, this week).
examples: I sent the email six months ago.
I've sent three emails this week and had no reply.
sections.tip: En Part 4 (key word transformation), 'It's the first time…' siempre lleva present perfect: It's the first time I've seen…

sections.title: Past continuous
sections.explain: Acción en progreso en un momento pasado, acción de fondo interrumpida por otra (past simple), situaciones que cambiaban, y hábitos molestos con always/constantly.
examples: We were talking about MP3s when Andrea walked in.
She was always borrowing my things without asking.

sections.title: Past perfect simple
sections.explain: Acción terminada ANTES de otro momento pasado. Muy común con when, by the time, after, already, just, never… before.
examples: By the time we arrived, the film had started.
Had you ever used a computer before you went to university?

sections.title: Past perfect continuous
sections.explain: Duración de una actividad hasta un momento pasado, o causa de una situación pasada.
examples: She had been writing for ten years before her first book was published.
His eyes were red because he'd been crying.

sections.title: Used to / would / be used to
sections.explain: used to + inf = hábitos Y estados pasados. would + inf = solo acciones repetidas (no estados). be/get used to + -ing = estar/acostumbrarse.
examples: I used to live in Bilbao. (estado: NO 'would live')
Every summer we would go to the beach.
It took me months to get used to living alone.
sections.tip: Trampa típica: 'He would be shy' ✗ → 'He used to be shy' ✓ (be es un estado).

u5.intro: Todas las formas de futuro y los matices entre ellas.

sections.title: Will
sections.explain: Predicciones basadas en opinión, decisiones espontáneas, ofertas, promesas y amenazas.
examples: I think it'll be a close match.
The phone's ringing — I'll get it!

sections.title: Be going to
sections.explain: Intenciones ya decididas y predicciones basadas en evidencia presente.
examples: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
I'm going to apply for that job.

sections.title: Present continuous y present simple
sections.explain: Present continuous = planes personales ya organizados. Present simple = horarios y calendarios fijos.
examples: I'm meeting Ane at six.
The train leaves at 6.15 tomorrow.

sections.title: Future continuous / perfect / perfect continuous
sections.explain: Continuous: en progreso en un momento futuro. Perfect: terminado antes de un momento futuro (by + tiempo). Perfect continuous: duración hasta un momento futuro.
examples: This time next week I'll be lying on a beach.
By June she'll have finished her degree.
By 2030 I'll have been working here for ten years.

sections.title: Time clauses
sections.explain: Después de when, as soon as, until, before, after, once, by the time: presente (o present perfect), NUNCA will.
examples: I'll call you as soon as I arrive. (no 'will arrive')
Don't leave until you've finished.

sections.title: Otras formas de futuro
sections.explain: be about to / be on the point of (inminente), be due to (programado), be to (anuncios formales), be bound to / be sure to (certeza). Futuro en el pasado: would, was going to, was about to.
examples: Hurry up, the film is about to start.
The Prime Minister is to visit Spain next month.
I thought she would call, but she didn't.

u7.intro: La voz pasiva, sus usos formales y las estructuras causativas.

sections.title: Cuándo usar la pasiva
sections.explain: Cuando el agente es desconocido, obvio o poco importante; para poner la información nueva al final; y para un estilo formal (informes, noticias).
examples: My bike was stolen last night.
The bridge was designed by a young engineer.

sections.title: Pasiva impersonal
sections.explain: It + pasiva + that clause, o sujeto + pasiva + to infinitive (to be / to have done). Verbos: say, believe, think, report, expect, consider, know.
examples: It is said that he is very rich.
He is said to have escaped through a window.
There are thought to be over 100 survivors.
sections.tip: Part 4 la pregunta muchísimo: People say he is… → He is SAID to be…

sections.title: Verbos con dos objetos
sections.explain: Pasiva con el objeto indirecto como sujeto (más común) o con el directo + to. Con explain, suggest, describe solo la forma con 'to'.
examples: Jill was given the tickets.
The tickets were given to Jill.
The problem was explained to us. (no 'We were explained')

sections.title: Evitar la pasiva
sections.explain: No se usa pasiva en perfect continuous ni future continuous: se usan expresiones como under construction, in progress, on display, under discussion. Verbos de estado (have, fit, lack, resemble) no suelen ir en pasiva.
examples: The bridge has been under construction for two years.

sections.title: Make, see, hear, help en pasiva
sections.explain: En activa van con infinitivo sin to; en pasiva llevan to.
examples: They made him rewrite it. → He was made to rewrite it.
She was heard to say she was leaving.

sections.title: Causativas
sections.explain: have/get + objeto + participio = encargar algo (o sufrir algo desagradable). get sb to do, have sb do = conseguir que alguien haga algo.
examples: I have my hair cut every six weeks.
She had her car stolen.
I got my brother to drive me to the airport.

u9.intro: Modales: habilidad, obligación, permiso, deducción y crítica.

sections.title: Habilidad
sections.explain: can/could; para un logro concreto en pasado: managed to / was able to (NO could en afirmativa). couldn't have + pp = imposibilidad pasada.
examples: Despite the storm, they managed to reach the summit.
I couldn't have finished without your help.

sections.title: Obligación y necesidad
sections.explain: must (obligación personal), have to (externa), mustn't (prohibición), don't have to / needn't (no hace falta). needn't have + pp = lo hice pero no era necesario; didn't need to = no lo hice porque no hacía falta.
examples: You mustn't park here.
I needn't have bought a ticket — it was free.
sections.tip: needn't have done vs didn't need to do es una trampa clásica de Part 4.

sections.title: Deducción y certeza
sections.explain: must (seguro que sí), can't/couldn't (seguro que no), may/might/could (posible), should/ought to (probable). Pasado: + have + pp.
examples: She isn't answering — she must be asleep.
He can't have seen the message.
The forecast is good, so it should be sunny tomorrow.

sections.title: Crítica y reproche
sections.explain: should have / ought to have + pp = crítica del pasado. could/might have + pp = podrías haber… will/would = hábitos molestos.
examples: You should have told me you were coming!
You might have warned me!
He will leave his socks on the floor.

sections.title: Permiso, peticiones y sugerencias
sections.explain: can/could/may para pedir permiso (may es más formal). Shall I/we… para ofrecer o sugerir. had better + inf = consejo fuerte.
examples: May I use your phone?
Shall we take a break?
You'd better hurry or you'll miss the bus.

u11.intro: Condicionales reales, irreales, mixtos e invertidos.

sections.title: Zero y first conditional
sections.explain: Zero: if/when + presente, presente (verdades generales). First: if + presente, will/imperativo/modal (situaciones posibles).
examples: If you heat ice, it melts.
If it rains tomorrow, we'll cancel the match.

sections.title: Second y third conditional
sections.explain: Second: if + past, would + inf (hipotético presente/futuro). Third: if + past perfect, would have + pp (pasado imposible). If I were you… = consejo.
examples: If I had more time, I'd learn the cello.
If she had studied harder, she would have passed.

sections.title: Mixed conditionals
sections.explain: Condición pasada → resultado presente: if + past perfect, would + inf. Condición presente → resultado pasado: if + past, would have + pp.
examples: If I hadn't missed the bus, I'd be at work now.
If I were braver, I would have said something.

sections.title: Condicionales invertidos
sections.explain: Más formales, sin if: Should + sujeto (first), Were + sujeto + to (second), Had + sujeto + pp (third). Negativo: Had it not been for…
examples: Should you need help, call me.
Were we to leave now, we'd arrive on time.
Had I known, I would have helped.
sections.tip: Muy útil en Writing para subir la nota de Language.

sections.title: Alternativas a if
sections.explain: unless (= if not), as/so long as, provided/providing (that), on condition that, supposing, otherwise, in case (por si acaso), but for / without + nombre.
examples: Take a coat in case it gets cold.
But for your help, I wouldn't have finished.
Book now, otherwise you won't get a seat.

u13.intro: Tiempo irreal: pasados que no hablan del pasado (wish, if only, it's time…).

sections.title: Wish / if only
sections.explain: wish + past = deseo sobre el presente. wish + past perfect = arrepentimiento sobre el pasado. wish + would = queja sobre algo/alguien que querríamos que cambiara. wish + could = habilidad.
examples: I wish I had more free time.
If only I hadn't said that!
I wish he wouldn't talk so loudly.
I wish I could play the piano.
sections.tip: No se usa wish + would con el mismo sujeto: 'I wish I would…' ✗

sections.title: It's (high/about) time
sections.explain: It's time + sujeto + past simple (ya deberíamos). It's time + to + inf (es el momento).
examples: It's high time we went home.
It's time to go.

sections.title: Would rather / would sooner
sections.explain: Mismo sujeto: would rather + inf. Distinto sujeto: would rather + sujeto + past (presente/futuro) o past perfect (pasado).
examples: I'd rather stay at home.
I'd rather you didn't smoke in here.
I'd rather you hadn't told her.

sections.title: As if / as though
sections.explain: Con pasado = comparación irreal. Con presente = posible/probable.
examples: He talks as if he knew everything. (no lo sabe)
It looks as if it's going to rain. (probable)

sections.title: Suppose / supposing / imagine / what if
sections.explain: Con pasado = hipótesis menos probable; con presente = más probable.
examples: Supposing you won the lottery, what would you do?
What if we miss the train?

u15.intro: Orden y posición de adjetivos y adverbios, comparaciones y adjetivos graduables.

sections.title: Orden de adjetivos
sections.explain: Opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → purpose + nombre.
examples: a lovely little old wooden cabin
a beautiful small black cat

sections.title: Posición de adjetivos
sections.explain: Algunos solo después del verbo: afraid, alike, alive, alone, asleep, awake, aware. Con as/so/too/how: adjetivo + a + nombre.
examples: The baby is asleep. (no 'an asleep baby')
I've never seen so beautiful a place.

sections.title: Adjetivos como nombres
sections.explain: the + adjetivo = grupo de personas, con verbo en plural.
examples: The poor need more help.
The French are proud of their cuisine.

sections.title: Graduables y no graduables
sections.explain: Graduables (tired, cold) con very, extremely, fairly. No graduables / extremos (exhausted, freezing, perfect, impossible) con absolutely, completely, utterly. really y quite sirven para ambos (quite + extremo = totalmente).
examples: He was absolutely exhausted.
This is utterly impossible.

sections.title: Comparaciones
sections.explain: much/far/a lot/slightly + comparativo; by far/easily + superlativo; not nearly as… as (mucha diferencia); nowhere near as; the + comparativo, the + comparativo.
examples: This flat is far bigger than mine.
It's by far the best restaurant in town.
The sooner, the better.

sections.title: Pares confusos
sections.explain: hard/hardly (casi no), late/lately (últimamente), near/nearly (casi), high/highly (muy), short/shortly (pronto), right/rightly (con razón).
examples: I could hardly hear him.
She is highly respected.
I'll be there shortly.

u17.intro: Oraciones de relativo, de participio y concesivas.

sections.title: Defining vs non-defining
sections.explain: Defining: información esencial, sin comas, se puede usar that y omitir el pronombre si es objeto. Non-defining: información extra, con comas, NO that, no se omite.
examples: The book (that) I bought is excellent.
My brother, who lives in Canada, is visiting us.

sections.title: Pronombres relativos
sections.explain: who (personas), which (cosas o toda la oración anterior), whose (posesión), whom (objeto, formal), where, when, why (the reason why). Preposición + whom/which = formal.
examples: He passed the exam, which surprised everyone.
That's the man to whom I spoke.

sections.title: Participle clauses
sections.explain: -ing (simultáneas o activas), having + pp (anterior), pp (pasiva). Pueden reducir relativas o expresar causa/tiempo. El sujeto debe ser el mismo.
examples: Walking down the street, I met an old friend.
Having finished the report, she went home.
The man living next door is a doctor.
sections.tip: Error típico: 'Walking down the street, a car hit me' ✗ (el coche no caminaba).

sections.title: Concesivas
sections.explain: although/though/even though + oración; despite/in spite of + nombre/-ing; however/no matter how + adj; much as; while/whereas para contraste; try as he might; adj + as/though + sujeto + verbo.
examples: Despite being tired, he kept working.
However hard he tried, he couldn't open it.
Tired as she was, she finished the race.

sections.title: Even if vs even though
sections.explain: even if = da igual que ocurra (hipotético). even though = a pesar de que (es un hecho).
examples: Even if it rains, we'll go.
Even though it was raining, we went.

u19.intro: Inversión, oraciones escindidas (cleft) y estructuras enfáticas.

sections.title: Inversión con adverbios negativos
sections.explain: Al empezar con never, rarely, seldom, hardly… when, no sooner… than, not only… but also, little, at no time, under no circumstances, on no account, in no way: auxiliar + sujeto.
examples: Never have I seen such a view.
Hardly had he left when it started to rain.
No sooner had she sat down than the phone rang.
Little did he know that…
sections.tip: Part 4 favorita: 'As soon as I arrived, …' → 'No sooner had I arrived than…'

sections.title: Only / not until
sections.explain: Only after/when/if/by…, Not until… + inversión en la oración principal.
examples: Only when he left did I realise the truth.
Not until the end did we understand.

sections.title: So / such inversión
sections.explain: So + adj + auxiliar + sujeto + that; Such + be + nombre + that.
examples: So rare is burglary here that people leave doors open.
Such was his anger that he couldn't speak.

sections.title: Cleft sentences
sections.explain: It + be + elemento enfatizado + who/that…; What + oración + be…; The reason why / The place where / The thing that…; All I want is…
examples: It was Maria who called the police.
What annoys me is his lateness.
All I need is a bit of peace.

sections.title: So / such / too / enough
sections.explain: so + adj/adv + that; such (a) + adj + nombre + that; too + adj + to; adj + enough + to; enough + nombre.
examples: It was such a long journey that we were exhausted.
She isn't old enough to drive.

sections.title: Contables e incontables
sections.explain: Incontables singulares: advice, information, furniture, news, luggage, equipment, research, progress, knowledge. Incontables plurales: clothes, scissors, goods, savings, surroundings, belongings. Algunos cambian de significado: paper / a paper, experience / an experience.
examples: Can you give me some advice? (no 'an advice')
My savings are in the bank.
The news is very bad.

sections.title: Cuantificadores
sections.explain: many/few/several/a number of + contable; much/little/a great deal of/an amount of + incontable; a lot of/plenty of/some/any/most/all con ambos. few/little = casi nada (negativo); a few/a little = algo (positivo).
examples: I have little money left, so I can't go out.
We have a little time, so let's continue.

sections.title: Artículo a/an
sections.explain: Primera mención, clasificar algo o a alguien, profesiones, 'por' (twice a week).
examples: She's an engineer.
I go running three times a week.

sections.title: Artículo the
sections.explain: Algo ya mencionado o específico, único (the sun, the government), superlativos, instrumentos musicales, the + adjetivo = grupo, nacionalidades, ríos, océanos, cordilleras, países con Republic/Kingdom/States.
examples: She plays the guitar.
the Pyrenees, the United Kingdom

sections.title: Sin artículo
sections.explain: Plurales e incontables en sentido general, la mayoría de países y ciudades, comidas, instituciones por su función (go to school/university/hospital/prison/church), medios de transporte con by.
examples: Children need love.
She's at university.
We went by train.

sections.title: Nombres colectivos
sections.explain: family, team, government, staff, audience: verbo en singular (grupo como unidad) o plural (miembros).
examples: My family is/are living in Gernika.

u23.intro: Verbo + -ing o infinitivo, cambios de significado y subjuntivo.

sections.title: Verbo + -ing
sections.explain: admit, avoid, can't help, can't stand, consider, deny, enjoy, feel like, finish, imagine, involve, mind, miss, postpone, practise, resent, risk, suggest, look forward to (to = preposición).
examples: She suggested going to the cinema.
I'm looking forward to seeing you.

sections.title: Verbo + to infinitive
sections.explain: afford, agree, arrange, decide, expect, fail, hope, manage, offer, plan, pretend, promise, refuse, seem, tend, threaten, wish.
examples: He refused to give the money back.
We can't afford to buy a house.

sections.title: Verbo + objeto + to / sin to
sections.explain: advise, allow, ask, encourage, force, invite, persuade, remind, tell, warn + obj + to. let, make (activa), see, hear, watch, help + obj + inf sin to.
examples: My teacher advised me to read more.
My parents don't let me stay out late.

sections.title: Cambio de significado
sections.explain: remember/forget + -ing (recuerdo del pasado) vs + to (no olvidar hacer). regret + -ing (arrepentirse) vs regret to inform (formal). stop + -ing (dejar) vs stop to (parar para). try + -ing (probar) vs try to (intentar). go on + -ing (seguir) vs go on to (pasar a). mean + -ing (implicar) vs mean to (tener intención).
examples: I remember meeting him at the party.
Remember to lock the door.
He stopped to smoke a cigarette.
sections.tip: Tipo de pregunta muy frecuente en Part 2 y Part 4.

sections.title: Subjuntivo
sections.explain: Después de verbos/adjetivos de importancia o sugerencia (insist, recommend, suggest, demand, essential, vital, important): sujeto + infinitivo sin to (o should + inf).
examples: The doctor recommended that she take more rest.
It's essential that he be informed.

sections.title: It preparatorio
sections.explain: it como objeto anticipado antes de un adjetivo + that/to: find/consider/think it + adj + to/that.
examples: I find it hard to concentrate.
I consider it odd that she didn't call.

u25.intro: Estilo indirecto y verbos de reporte.

sections.title: Backshift
sections.explain: present → past, past simple / present perfect → past perfect, will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to. No cambian: past perfect, would, could, should, might, ought to. No hace falta si la información sigue siendo verdad.
examples: 'I am tired.' → He said he was tired.
'I'll call you.' → She said she would call me.

sections.title: Tiempo y lugar
sections.explain: now → then, today → that day, yesterday → the day before / the previous day, tomorrow → the next/following day, ago → before, here → there, this → that.
examples: 'I saw her yesterday.' → He said he had seen her the day before.

sections.title: Preguntas y órdenes
sections.explain: Preguntas: orden afirmativo, sin do/does/did ni signo de interrogación; yes/no → if/whether. Órdenes: tell/ask/order + obj + (not) to.
examples: She asked me where I lived.
He asked if I had seen the film.
She told me not to touch it.

sections.title: Verbos de reporte + patrones
sections.explain: + to: agree, offer, promise, refuse, threaten. + obj + to: advise, encourage, invite, persuade, remind, warn. + -ing: admit, deny, recommend, suggest. + prep + -ing: accuse sb of, apologise for, blame sb for, congratulate sb on, insist on, object to.
examples: He accused me of stealing his wallet.
She apologised for being late.
He denied taking the money.
sections.tip: En Part 4 casi siempre aparece un verbo de reporte: aprende su patrón, no solo su significado.

sections.title: Suggest y recommend
sections.explain: suggest + -ing / suggest (that) + sujeto + (should) + inf. NUNCA suggest sb to do.
examples: She suggested going to the beach.
She suggested that he (should) take a break.
